subcategory: UNESCO Chandela Dynasty Nagara Temples & Erotic Sculptures
description: Constructed between 950 and 1050 CE by the Chandela dynasty, a world-famous group of 25 surviving sandstone temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Jain tirthankaras, celebrating human emotions, spirituality, and artistic sensuality.
why_visit: Admire the pinnacle of Indian temple architecture at Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, marvel at world-renowned intricate friezes depicting medieval life and aesthetics, and attend the annual February Dance Festival.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (6:00 AM - 6:00 PM; Western Group illuminated evenings)
activities: UNESCO Temple Tour; Architectural Photography; Sound and Light Show; Khajuraho Dance Festival
notes: Divided into Western, Eastern, and Southern groups; Western Group houses the most elaborately carved monuments.

subcategory: UNESCO 3rd Century BCE Buddhist Reliquary & Toranas
description: Commissioned by Emperor Ashoka the Great in the 3rd century BCE, the oldest stone structure in India, featuring an imposing 54-foot high hemispherical dome enshrining relics of the Buddha, encircled by four intricately carved ceremonial gateway toranas.
why_visit: Stand before the origin point of Buddhist monumental architecture, examine narrative Jataka carvings on the stone gateways, and explore ancient monastic ruins atop the quiet Sanchi hill.
activities: Buddhist Pilgrimage; Torana Relief Carving Study; Archaeological Museum Tour; Sunset Photography
notes: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1989; ASI museum at the base displays the lion capital of Sanchi.

subcategory: Seven-Storey Holkar Dynasty Timber & Stone Royal Residence
description: Built in 1747 by Malhar Rao Holkar, founder of the Holkar dynasty, a unique seven-storey royal residence blending Maratha, Mughal, and French styles, with lower floors of stone and upper floors constructed entirely of carved teakwood.
why_visit: Tour the ancestral palace of the beloved Maratha queen Devi Ahilyabai Holkar, admire wooden bracket carvings, and walk straight into the adjoining food and shopping streets of Sarafa and Khajuri Bazaar.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (10:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Light & Sound show at 6:30 PM)
activities: Palace Tour; Maratha Architecture Appreciation; Sound & Light Show; Nearby Sarafa Night Food Exploration
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: Central Indore / 2 km from Indore Junction
notes: Sarafa Night Food Market operates just 200 meters away after jewelry shops close at 8:30 PM.

subcategory: 8th-Century Hilltop Citadel & The Pearl of Indian Forts
description: Described by Mughal Emperor Babur as the 'pearl among fortresses of India', an impenetrable 8th-century plateau citadel featuring the dazzling turquoise-tiled Man Mandir Palace, Sas Bahu Temples, and colossal rock-cut Jain statues.
why_visit: Marvel at vibrant yellow and turquoise enameled duck and elephant tiles on Man Mandir Palace, visit the 9th-century Chaturbhuj Temple with the world's oldest written zero (0), and enjoy sunset views over Gwalior city.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (6:00 AM - 5:30 PM; Light and Sound show 7:30 PM)
activities: Citadel Rampart Walk; Man Mandir Palace Inspection; Rock-Cut Jain Statues Tour; Light & Sound Show
notes: Nightly sound & light show narrated in the voice of Amitabh Bachchan.

subcategory: Dakshinmukhi Shiva Jyotirlinga & Sacred Bhasma Aarti
description: One of the twelve sacred Shiva Jyotirlingas, unique for being South-facing (Dakshinmukhi) on the banks of the sacred Shipra River, world-famous for its dawn Bhasma Aarti performed using sacred cremation ash.
why_visit: Experience the intense spiritual power of the dawn Bhasma Aarti, witness the newly inaugurated grand Mahakal Lok corridor lined with 200 sculpted murals, and take sacred dips in the Shipra River.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round (Temple open 4:00 AM - 11:00 PM; Bhasma Aarti 4:00 AM - 6:00 AM)
activities: Bhasma Aarti Darshan; Mahakal Lok Corridor Walk; Shipra River Ram Ghat Holy Dip; Temple Worship
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 2 km from Ujjain Junction / 55 km from Indore
notes: Bhasma Aarti requires mandatory advance online booking on the official portal; traditional dress code enforced.

subcategory: Smoky Narmada River Gorge Waterfall & Pure Marble Canyons
description: A breathtaking 30-meter high plunge waterfall where the Narmada River narrows through shimmering white and tinted marble rock canyons, creating a permanent mist cloud resembling smoke (Dhuandhar).
why_visit: Take ropeway cable cars across the roaring smoky waterfall, cruise on wooden rowboats through 100-foot sheer white marble cliffs on full moon nights, and shop for carved marble souvenirs.
best_time_to_visit: October to April (Boating closed during monsoons)
activities: Ropeway Cable Car Ride; Marble Rocks Boat Safari; Waterfall Mist Viewing; Marble Handicraft Shopping
notes: Full moon boat rides between the Marble Rocks are an internationally acclaimed spectacle.

subcategory: 35-Metre Forest Gorge Cascade in Satpura Biosphere
description: Locally known as Jamuna Prapat, a perennial 35-meter mountain cascade falling through rugged sandstone ravines in the Satpura Biosphere Reserve, known as Bee Falls because from a distance the water stream hums like buzzing bees.
why_visit: Trek through sal forest steps down into the cool canyon, swim safely in natural rocky wading pools, and enjoy the refreshing microclimate of MP's only hill station.
activities: Waterfall Bathing; Forest Gorge Trekking; Nature Photography; Satpura Valley Sightseeing
notes: Involves climbing down approximately 300 paved stairs; carry water and avoid feeding monkeys.

subcategory: Inspiration for Kipling's Jungle Book & Barasingha Haven
description: Spanning 940 square kilometers of lush sal and bamboo forests and open meadows, the premier tiger reserve that inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book', famous for saving the hardground barasingha (swamp deer) from extinction.
why_visit: Experience world-class open gypsy safaris tracking Bengal tigers and leopards, watch herds of rare Barasingha swamp deer grazing on open savannah grasslands, and stay at eco-lodges.
activities: Tiger Safari; Wildlife Photography; Barasingha Spotting; Sunset Viewpoint Bamni Dadar Visit
notes: First tiger reserve in India to officially introduce a mascot: 'Bhoorsingh the Barasingha'.

subcategory: Highest Density of Royal Bengal Tigers in India
description: A 1,536-square-kilometer tiger reserve nestled around the ancient 2,000-year-old Bandhavgarh Fort hill, renowned for having the highest known density of Royal Bengal tigers anywhere in the world.
why_visit: Boasts the highest statistical probability of wild tiger sightings in India, explore ancient rock-cut caves and the 35-foot reclining Shesh Shaiya Vishnu idol deep inside the forest.
best_time_to_visit: October to June (Peak sightings March to May)
activities: Tiger Jeep Safari; Shesh Shaiya Vishnu Darshan; Bird Watching; Jungle Lodge Stay
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 100 km from Katni / 195 km from Jabalpur
notes: Divided into core zones (Tala, Magadhi, Khitauli); Tala zone houses the historic Shesh Shaiya statue.

subcategory: Bundela Dynasty Riverside Palaces & Royal Cenotaphs
description: Founded in the 16th century by Bundela chieftain Rudra Pratap Singh on an island in the Betwa River, an ethereal medieval complex featuring Raja Mahal, Jahangir Mahal, and 14 monumental royal chhatris (cenotaphs).
why_visit: Explore medieval courtyards with delicate turquoise and yellow ceramic tiles, admire original Bundela fresco paintings on palace ceilings, and photograph royal cenotaph reflections across the Betwa.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (9:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Light & Sound show 7:30 PM)
activities: Medieval Palace Exploration; Betwa River Kayaking; Cenotaph Photography; Ram Raja Temple Visit
notes: Orchha's Ram Raja Temple is the only temple in India where Lord Rama is worshipped as a reigning King with a police guard of honor.

subcategory: 15th-Century Floating Ship Palace Between Twin Lakes
description: Constructed during the reign of Sultan Ghiyas-ud-din Khilji, an enchanting 110-meter long two-storey palace built between two artificial lakes (Kapur Talao and Munj Talao), designed to appear as an enormous ship floating on water.
why_visit: Marvel at the ingenious medieval rain-fed water harvesting architecture, walk through domed pavilions and open terrace swimming pools, and explore nearby Roopmati Pavilion overlooking the Narmada valley.
best_time_to_visit: July to March (Spectacular lush greenery during monsoons)
activities: Floating Palace Photography; Mandu Monsoon Tour; Water Architecture Study; Baobab Tree Spotting
notes: Mandu is home to historic African Baobab trees brought by medieval Abyssinian traders.

subcategory: UNESCO 30,000-Year-Old Paleolithic Cave Paintings
description: An UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site featuring 750 prehistoric rock shelters nestled amidst sandstone cliffs in the Vindhya range, housing vibrant cave paintings dating from the Upper Paleolithic to the medieval era.
why_visit: See humanity's earliest art preserved in vivid natural red and white mineral pigments, depicting prehistoric hunting scenes, animal dances, and community rituals dating back 30,000 years.
activities: Paleolithic Rock Art Tour; Archaeological Exploration; Sandstone Cliff Hiking; Photography
notes: Auditorium Cave (Cave 3) features petroglyphs estimated to be among the oldest stone cupules in the world.

subcategory: Sacred Source of the Holy Narmada River & Maikal Hills
description: Perched at 1,048 meters altitude at the meeting point of the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, the sacred birthplace (Udgam) where the holy Narmada River originates from a sacred spring within an ancient white temple complex.
why_visit: Visit the exact sacred spring origin of the Holy Narmada, marvel at ancient 10th-century Kalachuri temples, explore pristine sal forests, and see nearby Kapildhara and Dudhdhara waterfalls.
hidden_gem_reason: A tranquil, deeply spiritual mountain pilgrimage site set amidst pristine sal forests, untouched by commercial tourist bustle.
activities: Narmada River Origin Darshan; Kalachuri Temple Exploration; Waterfall Treks; Herbal Forest Walks
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 120 km from Bilaspur / 220 km from Jabalpur
notes: Kapildhara Waterfall is just 6 km downstream where Narmada makes her first dramatic 100-foot plunge.

subcategory: Immersive Indigenous Tribal Art & Architectural Dwellings
description: An internationally acclaimed cultural museum in Shyamla Hills showcasing the indigenous life, cosmologies, myths, and life-size architectural dwellings of MP's prominent tribes (Gond, Bhil, Baiga, Korku, Sahariya).
why_visit: Walk through full-scale authentic tribal homes constructed by indigenous artisans using timber and mud, view mesmerizing mythic iron and clay installations, and watch live weekend tribal dance performances.
hidden_gem_reason: One of India's most brilliantly curated interactive museums, offering an immersive magical aesthetic unlike standard glass-case museums.
activities: Tribal Art Appreciation; Indigenous Architecture Walk; Cultural Performance Viewing; Craft Shopping
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: Adjacent to Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) in Bhopal
notes: Photography permitted; features a craft shop selling authentic Gond paintings and bell metal artifacts.

subcategory: Unspoiled wilderness and ancient temples await in Gyaraspur, a hidden gem in Madhya Pradesh's Satpura Hills.
description: Tucked away in the picturesque Satpura Hills of Madhya Pradesh, Gyaraspur is a trekkers' paradise that combines the thrill of adventure with the allure of Mother Nature's splendor. This off-the-beaten-path destination boasts an unspoiled wilderness, dotted with ancient temples and an abundance of flora and fauna. The terrain is a perfect blend of rugged hills, rolling forests, and winding rivers, making it an ideal setting for trekking, camping, and rock climbing. For those who seek solace in nature's beauty, Gyaraspur offers ample opportunities for bird watching, with many species of migratory birds calling this region home. The tranquil ambiance, combined with the warmth of local hospitality, makes Gyaraspur a must-visit destination for those seeking an immersive wilderness experience.
why_visit: Kanha Sakti Sthal Temple: A stunning ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Sati, perched on a rocky outcrop, offering breathtaking views of the surroundings.; Bhimbtek Caves: An ancient network of rock shelters dating back to the Mesolithic era, featuring fascinating cave paintings and carvings.; Satpura National Park: A protected area teeming with diverse wildlife, including tigers, leopards, and a wide variety of bird species.
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Guided Trek to the Kanha Sakti Sthal Temple: Embark on a moderately challenging trek to the temple, offering scenic views and opportunities to spot local wildlife.; Bird Watching at the Satpura National Park: Join a guided bird-watching tour to spot a wide variety of migratory birds, including species like the lesser florican and the sarus crane.; Rock Climbing at the Bhimbtek Caves: Challenge yourself with rock climbing at one of the oldest known shelters in the country.; Camping under the Stars: Set up camp near the Gyandev River and spend the night listening to the soothing sounds of nature and the rustling of leaves.
notes: Key photo spots: The Sunset Point at Kanha Sakti Sthal Temple: Watch the sunset over the rolling hills and valleys, creating a picturesque scene.; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry

subcategory: Discover the rugged charm of Tamia in Madhya Pradesh, where ancient rocks meet lush forests and adventure awaits.
description: Perched in the heart of Madhya Pradesh, Tamia is a trekker's paradise that boasts a unique blend of geological history, lush vegetation, and vibrant wildlife. This quaint town is nestled amidst the Satpura Range, a treasure trove of ancient volcanic rocks, towering sandstone cliffs, and dense forests, home to an array of exotic birds, monkeys, and even leopards. Tamia's breathtaking landscape is a testament to nature's untamed beauty, making it an irresistible destination for adventure-seekers and nature lovers alike. Whether you're an experienced trekker or a seasoned rock climber, Tamia offers a plethora of exciting activities that promise to leave a lasting impression.
why_visit: Trek through the rugged Satpura Range, which offers a range of trails for varying levels of experience, including the famous Dhoopgarh trek that takes you to the highest point in Madhya Pradesh.; Climb the towering Kanha Rock, a challenging climb that rewards you with breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape and a glimpse into the region's geological history.; Visit the ancient Kanha Caves, a network of massive sandstone caverns that have been shaped by millions of years of wind and water erosion.
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Go camping under the star-studded night sky at the Dhoopgarh campsite, which offers breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape.; Take a guided trek through the Satpura Range, led by expert guides who will share their knowledge about the region's history, geology, and wildlife.; Try your hand at rock climbing at Kanha Rock, or take a beginner's course with a certified instructor to learn the ropes.; Go on a nature walk through Tamia's forests and grasslands, where you can spot a variety of exotic bird species and maybe even a few leopards!
notes: Key photo spots: Capture stunning views of the Kanha Rock from the summit, where you can see the surrounding landscape stretching as far as the eye can see.; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry

subcategory: Where nature's majesty echoes the soul, within the ancient heart of Panna National Park.
description: Perched on the banks of the Ken River in Madhya Pradesh, India, Panna National Park is a treasure trove of rich biodiversity, offering an unparalleled wildlife experience. Steeped in history and spirituality, the park has been a haven for the local Sanchi tribes and various dynasties, leaving behind a legacy of ancient temples and mysterious ruins. Home to endangered Bengal tigers, majestic Barasingha, and an array of vibrant avifauna, Panna National Park has captivated the imagination of visitors and wildlife enthusiasts alike. As a sanctuary for the soul, the park invites you to embark on a serene jungle journey amidst majestic vistas, ancient temples, and the soothing melodies of the Ken River.
why_visit: Bengal Tiger, the majestic king of the forests, can be spotted roaming through the park's dense jungle terrain.; The temple of Pandav Falls is a sacred site for the local tribes, a testament to the ancient history that permeates the park.; Experience the majestic sight of 1000-year-old Rangnathji Temple in its grandeur amidst the lush greenery of the park.
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Embark on a boat safari across the serene Ken River, taking in the sights and sounds of the local wildlife.; Explore the hidden waterfalls of the park, where ancient rivers converge to create an oasis of tranquility.; Visit the majestic Rangnathji Temple amidst the lush greenery of the park, a glimpse into the region's ancient heritage.; Join a guided heritage walk through the park's scenic terrain, delving into the rich history and tribal culture that surrounds you.
notes: Key photo spots: Saddle Point Waterfall - capture the stunning sight of the waterfall cascading down amidst lush green jungles.; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry

subcategory: Discover the serenity of the Vindhya Hills in Maheshwar, where ancient temples and treacherous terrain beckon the adventurer.
description: Situated on the banks of the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh, Maheshwar is a scenic hill town surrounded by the rugged grandeur of the Vindhya Hills. This ancient pilgrimage center boasts a rich cultural heritage, characterized by intricately carved temples of Maratha and Rajput architecture. As a trekker, you'll be treated to an array of challenging trails, each offering a unique perspective on this enchanting landscape. Whether you're scaling the towering cliffs, camping under star-studded skies, or bird-watching through the lush forests, Maheshwar's natural splendor and spiritual essence will leave you enchanted.
why_visit: The stunning Jaleshwar Temple, a 16th-century marvel perched atop a granite outcrop, offering breathtaking views of the Narmada.; The picturesque Kajli Puliya Bridge, a rustic, ancient suspension bridge spanning the river, providing a photographer's paradise.; The ancient fortifications and ruins of the erstwhile Maheshwar kingdom, a testament to the town's rich history and strategic importance.
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Embark on the challenging trek to the top of Bhedaghat, a rugged, granite monolith offering stunning views of the surrounding landscape.; Camp under the stars in the picturesque forest clearings near the banks of the Narmada River.; Partake in the traditional 'Shuklavaar' festivities, a centuries-old celebration commemorating the sacred Shukla Paksha.; Take a thrilling rock climbing excursion up the towering cliffs of the Vindhya Hills, amidst ancient temples and scenic vistas.
notes: Key photo spots: The sun-kissed Ghats at Maheshwar, offering a photographer's dream of golden light, majestic temple silhouettes, and serene river scenes.; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry

subcategory: A historical fort town of ancient monuments, Rajput heritage, and world-renowned handloom weavers.
description: Chanderi is an ancient town situated in the Ashoknagar district of Madhya Pradesh, nestled between hills, lakes, and forests. Renowned for its rich Bundela Rajput history, Islamic architecture, and Jain temples, the town has been an important trade route since the 11th century. Today, it is famous both for its towering Chanderi Fort and its centuries-old handloom weaving tradition that produces the luxurious, sheer Chanderi silk sarees.
why_visit: Chanderi Fort (Kirti Durg): A 15th-century hilltop fortress offering panoramic views of the town.; Badal Mahal Gate: The iconic, intricately carved Mughal-style archway that serves as the symbol of Chanderi.; Pranpur Weaving Village: An eco-tourism craft village where visitors can see local weavers create sheer Chanderi fabrics.
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Explore Chanderi Fort and Badal Mahal Gate; Visit Pranpur craft village to learn handloom weaving; Walk through the rock-cut gateway of Kati Ghati; Visit Koshak Mahal and Shehzadi Ka Roza monuments
notes: Key photo spots: Badal Mahal Gate framed against the blue sky; Local culinary highlights: Bundelkhandi Thali, Bhutte Ka Kees, Mawa Bati

subcategory: Unveil the hidden gems of Central India's unexplored wilderness at the Phen Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh
description: Nestled in the heart of the Satpura Range, the Phen Sanctuary is a relatively uncharted destination for adventure-seekers and nature enthusiasts. Covering an impressive 217 square kilometers, this protected area is a melting pot of diverse flora and fauna, with a rich tapestry of deciduous forests, scrublands, and meadows. Visitors can embark on invigorating nature walks, guided treks, and thrilling wildlife excursions to discover the sanctuary's unspoiled natural beauty.
why_visit: Observe the majestic Barasingha, a critically endangered species of swamp deer, in their natural habitat; Explore the stunning Khurkhanda waterfalls, a breathtaking sight that epitomizes the sanctuary's natural splendor; Engage in bird watching activities to spot the elusive Crested Honey Buzzard, a rare sighting in Indian skies
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Take a guided nature walk to spot exotic bird species like the Orange-breasted Pitta and the White-naped Tit; Join a guided camping excursion to experience the thrill of living amidst the wilderness; Try your hand at wildlife photography to capture the majestic beauty of the sanctuary's inhabitants; Visit the nearby Balaghat region to experience the rich cultural heritage of the local tribes
notes: Key photo spots: The scenic viewpoint of the Mand River, where the river flows through the stunning granite formations; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry

subcategory: A deep horseshoe-shaped valley rich in tribal heritage and rare herbs.
description: Patalkot Valley is a deep, horseshoe-shaped valley located in the Chhindwara district of Madhya Pradesh. Carved out by the Dudhi River, the valley is located at a depth of nearly 1,200 to 1,500 feet, making it so remote that its tribal inhabitants (mostly Bharia and Gond tribes) lived in complete isolation for centuries. Patalkot is renowned for its spectacular landscape, rich tribal culture, and as a treasure trove of rare medicinal plants.
why_visit: Spectacular views of the horseshoe valley from the top edge; Authentic Bharia and Gond tribal villages untouched by modern urbanization; Incredible collection of rare medicinal herbs and traditional remedies
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
best_time_to_visit: October to March & July to September (monsoon lushness)
activities: Trekking down into the valley to visit tribal hamlets like Gaildubba; Learning about traditional tribal medicine from local healers (Bhumkas); Attending local tribal markets and witnessing traditional dance forms; Landscape photography of the steep valleys and misty cliffs
notes: Key photo spots: Patalkot Valley viewpoint at sunrise; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry

subcategory: Discover the uncharted charm of Burhanpur, a tranquil haven amidst the Tapti River in southern Madhya Pradesh.
description: Burhanpur, nestled in the eastern slopes of the Satpura Range, is a serene hill station awaiting exploration. This quaint town has been a gateway between Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh for centuries, boasting a rich history that reflects in its architectural marvels and archaeological remnants. As you wander through Burhanpur's lush forests and picturesque villages, immerse yourself in the local culture, and experience the simple joys of rural life. The mountainous terrain and surrounding wilderness make it an ideal destination for trekkers, nature enthusiasts, and photographers alike.
why_visit: The Kala Kheria Bird Sanctuary, a treasure trove of avifauna, where over 200 species of birds find refuge.; The 17th-century Bhadresvar Temple, an impressive example of Maratha and Burhanpur-style architecture.; The ancient Dara Shikoh Raika Tomb, a poignant tribute to Mughal royalty.
hidden_gem_reason: An offbeat, serene destination in Madhya Pradesh offering authentic natural vistas and cultural experiences far from heavy tourist crowds.
activities: Embark on a trek to the picturesque village of Chikhaldara, perched on a hilltop, offering breathtaking vistas.; Take a guided nature walk through the forest, discovering the hidden gems of the region, including medicinal plants and local wildlife.; Visit the local market, where you can sample local delicacies, purchase handicrafts, and interact with the friendly locals.; Capture the essence of Burhanpur through photography, with scenic vistas of the surrounding hills and valleys.
notes: Key photo spots: The Kala Kheria Bird Sanctuary's dawn bird-watching session, when the sky comes alive with chirping birds.; Local culinary highlights: Local Traditional Thali, Spicy Curry
